title: Choose the landing page structure — round 2 (safer)
question: Fresh hand, steered safer per your re-roll. Visual system still fixed (navy / vermilion / mint, Manrope).

options.label: The Long Read
options.thesis: No card grids — the page reads as one continuous editorial narrative, headline-led, built for a visitor who wants to be convinced by argument, not scanned by a stranger.
options.viewport: A single centered text column, inline product shots breaking the flow at moments of proof, no repeating card shells; typographic rhythm alone creates hierarchy.
options.risk: Loses the scanability a first-time, skeptical fintech visitor often wants; a long unbroken column can feel like reading, not deciding.

raised.raise: Every parsed-entry example shown is a real, distinct variation (different merchant, amount, category) — never uniform mock rows repeated for tidiness.
New entries visibly displace what's above them as they arrive — nothing sits static once it lands.
Every stat and total carries an exact value pinned to it — no rounded or vague claims.
"Connect your phone" is the one action that visibly transforms the whole page from scattered to organized — dramatize that as a single motion, not a static before/after graphic.

options.label: The Comparison
options.thesis: Costiq's case is made by contrast: a comparison table (Costiq / spreadsheet / manual apps) sits where a feature grid usually goes.
options.viewport: Hero as usual, then an early comparison table (manual entry, categorization, budgets, review, cross-device) scored across three columns, before deeper feature explanation.
options.risk: Comparison tables can look defensive/combative if the other columns aren't handled fairly.

options.label: The Persona Switch
options.thesis: A toggle near the top lets a visitor pick who they are, reflowing proof and copy beneath to match before converging on one CTA.
options.viewport: Hero with a 2-3 way segmented control (e.g. salaried / freelancer / household); sections below swap emphasis per selection; pricing/CTA stay constant.
options.risk: No confirmed distinct personas in product truth — this invents segmentation the product hasn't validated, and the wrong personas could mis-target the copy.

options.label: The Paired Spread
options.thesis: The page paginates as mirrored two-panel spreads — an SMS pose on one side answered by its parsed result on the other — scroll-snapped like turning a page, not scrolled like a feed.
options.viewport: Full-height spreads, each a left/right pair: raw SMS or a feature claim on one side, its Costiq-side result mirrored on the other, hairline rule down the seam; pagination replaces continuous scroll.
options.case: Beats The Long Read on both axes — same editorial ambition, but the mirrored pose/answer pairing makes the mechanism concrete at every step instead of relying on prose alone, while staying more visually distinctive than a plain column.
options.risk: Scroll-snap pagination can feel restrictive on mobile if panel pairs don't collapse cleanly to a stacked single column.

options.label: The Level Row
options.thesis: Category budgets render as a row of real needle meters that lean toward red as spend approaches the limit.
options.case: Holds product clarity strongly — a leaning needle communicates "approaching your limit" more viscerally than a flat progress bar — but the recording-studio reference is a mild audience stretch for an everyday UPI user.
options.kept: True ballistic motion (needles ease/overshoot like real levels, not instant fills) as the proof-of-automatic detail.

options.label: Silkscreen Loft
options.case: Fuses poorly — repeated off-register portrait editions have no product-clarity link to expense tracking.
options.kept: Real, distinct variation between shown examples rather than uniform mock rows.

options.label: Ebru Basin
options.case: Fuses poorly — a fluid-displacement simulation is a large lift with weak payoff for "automatic categorization."
options.kept: New entries visibly displace what's above them as they arrive.

options.label: Tensegrity Column
options.case: Fuses poorly — abstract engineering metaphor, weak mainstream audience identification, costly constraint-graph build.
options.kept: Exact values pinned to every stat and total via leader-line style precision.

options.label: Drawcord Cape
options.case: Fuses poorly — a cloth-physics simulation is a large lift and a stretch association for a finance product.
options.kept: The whole product framed as one visible transformation (connect → organized) in a single dramatized motion.
